summary: Iteration 44: frontend-only check of PR #11 'The Living Scripture & Personal Bookshelf' (web preview at 390x844 and 360x640, light mode and dark mode via prefers-color-scheme). Node suite: 34/34 pass. tsc --noEmit is clean. ESLint shows 1 warning (import/first in app/living/[id].tsx:19). WORKING: The library shows all 18 books: lexicon, timeline, media, the 7 open-living-* volumes, way, mine, favBible, favLessons, photos, units, prayer and terms. There is only one 'Auf den Spuren Jesu' book, and the local library-cover.jpg still renders. The entry counts add up to 223 (106+26+16+30+14+14+17). Volume pages: each cover uses contain and loads. Search works for German ('Liebe' gives 4 results), transliteration (agape, chesed), Greek script (ἀγάπη) and Hebrew script (חסד), each giving exactly 1 result; nonsense text shows the empty state. Group chips filter correctly (Hebrew 50, Greek 50, Aramaic 6). The detail screen works. Tapping a reference such as Rut 1,8 opens /bible?b=Rut&ch=1&v=8. Prev/next work, and the first entry has no prev button. An invalid id shows a 'nicht gefunden' message. Hebrew and Aramaic (with niqqud) render RTL, Greek renders LTR, and there are no missing-glyph boxes in light or dark mode at either size. Jesus volume: the journey button opens the /intro 15-station screen, the psalms button opens /psalms-jesus (which has a new open-jesus-teachings button back to the volume), and the parables button opens /world/parables. Trees: all 14 entries render diagram lines and lexicon links (tree-4 links abraham, sara, isaak), and the links open /lexicon/abraham. Bookshelf edit mode, tried on lexicon, media, mine, terms and history: size, shelf, order arrows, palette colour, hex colour (invalid '#12345G' disables Apply; '#f4e5bd' gets black ink), original colour and icon all work. Saved changes survive a reload, and all 18 books are still present. Cancel throws away the draft. Reset asks for confirmation and brings back the default shelf. Backups: the JSON export (biblia-lernstand-*.json) contains settings.libraryLayout with colour and icon, and so does the full backup (biblia-vollsicherung-*.json). Importing the JSON restores the custom layout. 'Jetzt sichern' followed by restoring the weekly backup brings back the custom layout after a reset. Regression: library tabs mine, prayer, photos and terms open their sections, /media loads, and no console errors appeared in any run. ISSUES are all cosmetic or regressions of the original Jesus book. No deprecated Expo packages were found.

ui_bugs.issue:
Long one-word titles break in the middle of the word at 390 and 360 widths: 'Unsichtbar/e Welt', 'Stammbäu/me', 'Bibelgeschi/chte' (once history is moved next to another book). At 360 it gets worse: 'Unsichtba/re Welt', 'Stammbä/ume'. On web, adjustsFontSizeToFit is ignored and the 22px titleLarge does not fit a book about 150px wide. Fix: add explicit '
' or soft hyphens to the short titles (for example 'Unsicht-
bare Welt', 'Stamm-
bäume', 'Bibel-
geschichte'), as the existing books already do ('Hören &
Sehen', 'Studien-reise'), or use a smaller font for long titles. Reference: frontend/app/(tabs)/library.tsx:152, frontend/src/components/Bookshelf.tsx:74

The title is cut off as 'Auf den Spuren ...'. Two changes cause this: Book.tsx now uses numberOfLines={large ? 2 : 3} (it used to be 3 for all books), and the new title 'Auf den Spuren Jesu' has no '
'. The old book used 'Auf den Spuren
Jesu' and fit. Fix: use the title 'Auf den Spuren
Jesu', or allow 3 lines again. Reference: frontend/app/(tabs)/library.tsx:152, frontend/src/components/Bookshelf.tsx:74

issues: The existing 'Auf den Spuren Jesu' book changed its look and place without being asked. Its theme went from BOOK_THEMES.journey to favBible (red), its icon from sunrise to sun, its subtitle from '15 Stationen' to '30 Einträge', and it moved from the 'way' shelf to deep2. Tapping it now opens /living/jesus instead of /intro (the journey is still one tap away inside). The user asked for colours to stay unchanged, so the main agent should decide whether to keep the old journey theme and sunrise icon as the defaults. Reference: library.tsx:150-152, library-layout.ts:22

The new volumes reuse existing book themes, which gives several pairs the same colour: words = lexicon, history = prayer, jesus = favBible, trees = way, unseen = timeline, thread = favLessons, symbols = units. Books on different shelves look identical, which makes them harder to tell apart (low priority).
testID changed from open-jesus-journey to open-living-jesus. No code or tests reference the old ID, but note it for future test scripts.

The name matcher in lexiconFor uses a whole-word regex on the first word of each article title, so possessive forms are missed. 'Jakobs Söhne' (tree-6) does not link jakob, and 'Mann Marias' (tree-12) does not link maria. Results are also capped at 8, so tree-12 drops later names. Minor content gap. Reference: app/living/[id].tsx:18

action_items: Fix the mid-word breaks in large book titles: add explicit line breaks or hyphens to the volume short titles (Unsichtbare Welt, Stammbäume, Bibelgeschichte) or shrink the font for long titles.
Fix the truncated 'Auf den Spuren ...' title: use 'Auf den Spuren\nJesu', or set numberOfLines back to 3 for large books in Bookshelf.tsx.
Decide whether the 'Auf den Spuren Jesu' book should keep its original theme (BOOK_THEMES.journey), icon (sunrise) and default shelf, to honour 'colors unchanged'.
Optional: make lexiconFor match German possessive forms (Jakobs, Marias) and move the import at app/living/[id].tsx:19 to the top of the file (ESLint import/first).

Optional: the open-jesus-teachings button on /psalms-jesus uses router.push, so going living/jesus → psalms → living/jesus keeps adding screens to the back stack. Consider router.back() when the previous screen is that volume.
critical_code_review_comments: library-layout.ts: normalizeLibraryLayout handles bad, duplicate and unknown entries well and appends new default books, so no book can disappear. shiftLibraryBook only swaps neighbours on the same shelf. This was verified in the UI.

PersonalBookshelf: the edit sheet is driven by a draft, and Cancel and Reset both act only on the draft until Save. While editing, tapping a book still plays the 'pull-out' open animation before the sheet opens. This is harmless but adds a small delay.
settings.libraryLayout goes through the existing settings spread in progress-logic.ts:142, so export, import, full backup and guardian restore all keep it. This was verified end-to-end.
frontend/yarn.lock is untracked (it appeared this session). package.json is unchanged, so no new dependencies were added.

The Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek text uses the system font stack with no bundled font. Web rendering is fine. On older Android devices without Noto Hebrew, check on a real device that niqqud displays correctly.
updated_files: /app/tests/ui_helpers_bookshelf.py (new test helper only; no app code changed)

success_rate.frontend: 95% - all functional flows pass; 2 cosmetic title issues and 1 design regression on the Jesus book

seed_data_creation: None. Every UI run used a fresh browser context with its own localStorage, and no user data was changed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Close the intro with 'Überspringen' and then 'Bibel entdecken'. Guardian localStorage values are not plain JSON, so check libraryLayout with page.expect_download on export-button or full-backup-button. In bookshelf edit mode, books are opened with their normal testIDs (open-*, library-tab-*). Sheet chips sometimes need scrollIntoView before clicking. Shelf rows are split by weight (large 1.5, medium 1.5, small 1; max 3 per row), so their testIDs become shelf-<id>-1 and so on. The theme-dark chip does not work on web (known since iteration 31, react-native-web has no setColorScheme), so use page.emulate_media(color_scheme='dark') instead.
rca_of_issue: Title truncation: Bookshelf.tsx changed numberOfLines for large books from 3 to 2, and the Jesus title lost its explicit '\n'. Mid-word breaks: on web, react-native-web ignores adjustsFontSizeToFit and breaks long words to wrap, so long single-word titles at 22px split inside the word in books about 150px wide.
